documents.title: Board Meeting Intimation for Consideration Of Audited Financial Results For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026
Disclosure Of Information Under Regulation 30 Of SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015, Reply To Clarification Sought On Spurt In Volume Of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited Shares
Clarification sought from Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its financial and operational performance for Q4 and FY26, achieving a highest-ever annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and record production across several value-added products like diesel, petrol, and LPG. Management highlighted a debt-equity ratio of 0.18 and noted that ongoing expansion projects, including Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS and retail outlets, are underway. The company declared a total dividend of INR 62 per share for the year, including a recommended final dividend of INR 54 per share. Despite ongoing global uncertainties and geopolitical events, management expressed confidence in sustaining operational momentum and focusing on capital discipline. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported its financial and operational performance for Q4 and FY 2024-25, highlighting resilient crude throughput and improved efficiency despite lower international product cracks compared to the previous year.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern market has a clear shortfall in Motor Spirit (MS) where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Motor Spirit demand growth in the southern market is projected around 4%-5% compared to the national growth projection of 6%.
demand_outlook.quote: As far as others are concerned, we have seen the southern market to be mostly aligned to the national growth projection. Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%.

demand_outlook.claim: High-Speed Diesel (HSD) demand growth in the southern market is forecast at 3% growth compared to 2.5% nationally.
demand_outlook.quote: HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The capex for the financial year was INR 856 crores compared to INR 673 crores previously.
capex_expansion.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capex_expansion.claim: Project execution for Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS has started in full swing with all approvals in place.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The retail outlet endeavor has started and the financial year 2026-27 will see commissioning out of them.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project size is INR 1,600 crores and the retail outlet project is INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL spent Rs. 673 crores as capital expenditure during the financial year 2024-25.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery basin refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

margins_costs.claim: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM for quarter 4 was 10.3 dollars per barrel.
The forex loss for the quarter was approximately INR 200 crores and for the whole year around INR 350 crores.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: The Gross Refining Margin (GRM) for the full year 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: The Gross Refining Margin for Q4 was $6.22 per barrel compared to $7.7 per barrel in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel. Again, if I compare the previous year same quarter, it was $7.7 per barrel, but if I compare it to Singapore benchmark, which was only $3.1 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for the fourth quarter stood at $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: On an overall annual basis, inventory resulted in a loss of $0.06 per barrel, or Rs. 40 crores.
margins_costs.quote: But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved the highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, which is equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: In quarter 4, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The capacity of pharma-grade Hexane is 60 following the doubling of capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: It was 30, now the capacity is 60.

orders_capacity.claim: The new LOBS unit will add a capacity of 250,000 KTPA in Group 2 and Group 3.
orders_capacity.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput for Q4 was 2.974 MMT, representing 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.18 at a gross level compared to 0.39 last year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18. Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: On a gross basis, borrowings are INR 1,900 crores and on a net basis, it is INR 973 crores with a net debt ratio of 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores. If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR 62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-to-equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Total absolute debt stood at Rs. 3,100 crores as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: Net worth stood at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge to operations and earnings.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the INR 2,000 crores outlay for the LOBS and retail outlet projects will happen over 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the ongoing study for potential low-cost debottlenecking will get completed in the coming financial year 2026-27.
management_commitments.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.

management_commitments.claim: Normal maintenance capital expenditure for the next two years is projected to be in the range of Rs. 200 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
